A dusty desert main-street town baking under a white sky, one long rutted road lined with sun-bleached false-front timber buildings, warped boardwalks, a cracked water trough, and dry scrubland stretching flat to the horizon.

A muddy rain-churned boomtown knee-deep in spring muck, planks thrown across the street as makeshift crossings, canvas-roofed storefronts wedged between raw lumber frames, wagon ruts flooded to the axle, grey clouds pressing low overhead.

A gold-rush mining town clinging to a steep Sierra hillside, buildings stacked in precarious tiers along a single switchback street, timber flumes cutting across the slope, lantern light glowing from tent-and-board storefronts hammered into the rock face.

A cattle-town railhead sprawling at the end of a newly laid track, a wide dusty main street running hard past saloons and a land office toward the stench of packed timber stockyards, cattle pens stretching east in long parallel rows.

A sun-baked adobe pueblo town of the Southwest, thick-walled earthen buildings rising square and low around a central plaza, a hand-dug well at its center, dried chiles hanging in red ropes from vigas above doorways of heavy weathered wood.

A weathered clapboard town alone on the open plains, grey-painted storefronts facing each other across a wide dirt street, a windmill turning slowly at the far end, nothing beyond the last building but flat tallgrass prairie running to a distant treeline.

A town wedged at the mouth of a red-rock canyon, buildings pressed close between sheer sandstone walls that glow amber in the afternoon sun, the single main street narrowing as it pushes deeper into the cleft, shadows arriving early and hard.

A river-crossing town built around a busy ferry landing, a short grid of mercantile buildings and a rough-timber tavern fronting the brown water, thick rope hawsers anchored to iron posts, mule teams waiting on the muddy bank for the flat-bottomed barge.

A snowbound mountain mining camp buried to its eaves in late-winter drifts, log-and-board buildings hunched together along a cleared-out lane, smoke rising from iron stovepipes, a frozen creek edging the camp, pine ridges black against a pale cold sky.

A sun-blasted Mexican-border town straddling a dry arroyo, whitewashed adobe walls crumbling at their corners, a central street of packed caliche dust, an old stone mission at the far end, mesquite and ocotillo crowding the broken low wall around the settlement.

A lawless crossroads trading post where two rutted trails meet on open grassland, a single long low log building with a covered porch, a hitching rail running its full length, animal hides stretched on the outer wall, no other structure visible in any direction.

A prosperous brick-and-timber boomtown at its noisy peak, a wide main street of two-storey commercial buildings with glass-front windows and painted signs, gas lamps on iron posts, a busy bank on the corner, a freshly graded side street leading to a new lumber yard.

A high-desert silver-rush town perched on an alkaline flat, temporary board-and-batten storefronts in a single crooked row, a stamp mill thundering on the hill above, grey tailings spilling down the slope, jackrabbits darting beneath the gap-plank boardwalk.

A timber-trade town built in a Pacific Northwest river valley, wide unpaved streets slicked with bark and sawdust, enormous log piles stacked beside a steam-powered mill, workers' bunkhouses in raw pine behind the main street, dense fir forest pressing close on three sides.

A freighting hub town on a high-plains crossroads, oversized wagon yards taking up half the settlement, heavy Conestoga wagons ranked in rows, a long low warehouse with loading docks, wide streets built to turn a six-mule team without scraping the storefronts.

A remote alkali-flat desert outpost serving the stage line, a single row of thick-walled adobe buildings behind a low wall, a covered well in the yard, a stone corral for relay horses, the land absolutely flat and pale and empty in every direction.

A riverside placer-mining camp become a proper town, a muddy main street running parallel to a gravel-bar creek, sluice equipment rusting at the bank, weathered canvas storefronts giving way to freshly built timber ones, cottonwoods lining the water's edge in gold-green leaf.

A coal-camp town hollowed into a Wyoming bluff, company-built identical clapboard houses in a rigid grid, a company store dominating the main street, black coal dust staining every surface, the dark mouth of the mine shaft visible above the roofline on the hill.

A wind-hammered northern plains town enduring a dry summer, every false-front bleached near white, the street bare hard dirt with tumbleweed lodged against the boardwalk posts, a grain elevator looming at the rail spur, the sky enormous and cloudless overhead.

A spring-fed oasis town in the Sonoran desert, a handful of thick adobe buildings arranged around a reed-fringed pool, a shaded zaguán passageway through the main building, low ocotillo-post corrals beyond, the surrounding desert a blinding sweep of saguaro and bare gravel.

A mountain-pass toll town controlling the only practical route through the range, a tight cluster of stone-and-log buildings on either side of the rutted pass road, a heavy gate and toll booth, pine-slope walls rising steeply to either side, snow still patching the high ridges.

A hide-and-tallow coastal California town, long low adobes with red clay-tile roofs arranged around a dusty plaza, a crumbling mission arcade along one side, oxcart ruts radiating from the center, live oaks casting deep shade over the whitewashed outer walls.

A railroad construction camp grown into a rough town, a chaotic double row of portable wood-frame buildings paralleling the new graded roadbed, steel rail stacked in fields behind, a water tower over the tracks, the whole settlement smelling of grease, coal smoke, and fresh timber.

A saloon-and-gambling district town on a flat Kansas prairie, wide main street built deliberately broad for drovers, every second building a saloon with a lit porch lantern, a jailhouse of iron-strapped timber at the end, cattle dust still hanging in the evening air.

A remote desert water-stop town beside a natural spring, three or four thick-walled stone buildings around a central cistern, a low adobe wall penning the spring source, the trail in deep with hoof prints, jagged volcanic ridgeline cutting the skyline behind the settlement.
